summary_en: Updated medium-term management plan targeting ROE of 6.0% or higher and PBR of 1.0x or above by fiscal year ending March 2029, with sales of 15.0 billion yen and operating margin of 5.3%. Current five-year average ROE stands at 2.5% and PBR at 0.77x, reflecting insufficient market recognition of growth strategy.
title_en: Response to Realize Management Conscious of Cost of Capital and Stock Price (Update)
translation_en_brief:
Mitsuboshi has updated its capital cost and stock price awareness management framework in response to persistent undervaluation. The company's five-year average PBR stands at 0.77x, with the most recent fiscal year ending March 2026 declining to 0.43x despite recovery in profitability. Five-year average ROE is 2.5%, though fiscal 2026 improved to 3.5% as net income attributable to parent company shareholders reached 246 million yen.

The updated medium-term management plan through fiscal year ending March 2029 targets PBR of 1.0x or higher and ROE of 6.0% or higher. Financial targets include sales of 15.0 billion yen, operating profit of 800 million yen, and operating margin of 5.3%. The company attributes persistent undervaluation to insufficient market recognition of its long-term growth strategy and future earnings expansion potential, alongside capital efficiency improvements needed.

To achieve these targets, the company will enhance profitability management by incorporating capital cost awareness into decision-making processes, utilizing metrics including ROIC alongside ROE, and emphasizing the relationship between expected returns and cost of capital in capital allocation. The company will strengthen existing business competitiveness while pursuing business portfolio expansion through M&A and strategic partnerships, with rigorous evaluation of target profitability, growth potential, synergies, payback periods, and capital efficiency. Enhanced engagement with shareholders and investors and improved disclosure aim to ensure appropriate market valuation of corporate value. ESG principles—including renewable energy adoption, disaster resilience, recycling, automation, supply chain optimization, intellectual property development, work-life reform, talent development, internal control enhancement, and compliance—will be integrated into core management strategy.
